findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has wrong substring indices and inverted return logic
findings.body:
Two bugs in the new isAccessTokenId matcher combined defeat its purpose of verifying the grant-type shortcut:

  1. Wrong substring indices. The encoded prefix format is sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantType(2), so the grant shortcut is at indices 4..5 (substring(4, 6)). The code uses substring(3, 5), which captures the second token-type char plus the first grant-type char (e.g. for "onrtac" it returns "ta" instead of "ac").
  2. Inverted return: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` accepts any token whose (wrong) substring is not equal to the expected grant shortcut, and rejects the ones whose substring accidentally equals it. For the current shortcuts ("ac","cc","ro","rt","ci","dg") substring(3,5) never equals a 2-letter grant shortcut by accident, so the matcher silently passes for any well-formed encoded id regardless of actual grant type.

Consequence: any test using expectCodeToToken / expectDeviceCodeToToken / expectRefresh / expectAuthReqIdToToken does not actually assert the grant-type shortcut, so regressions where the encoder emits the wrong grant shortcut will not be caught.

findings.title: Null-check parameter is wrong: checks grantType but message says rawTokenId
Public copy constructor Context(Context) was silently removed
findings.body: The diff deletes the previously existing public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (public static class in a public interface). Any external or subclass code that did `new Context(existingContext)` will fail to compile against this SPI after the change. The PR does not mention this as a breaking change and there is no replacement for the copy semantics that the removed constructor provided (copying all transitive state of an existing context). At a minimum the removal needs to be called out and ideally the constructor should be preserved (extended to also propagate grantType).

findings.title: New abstract method getShortcut() is a breaking SPI change for third-party grant factories
findings.body: The interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` gains the abstract method `String getShortcut();`. The PR updates every in-tree implementation, but any third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` provider will fail to load after this change because it no longer implements all interface methods. Such a breaking change should at least ship with a default implementation in the interface (e.g. returning the grant id truncated or the first two letters) to preserve backward compatibility, or be announced in upgrade/migration docs.
